Header. url: rights: public_reference why: Details a top-down, root cause analysis framework for diagnosing performance drops in e-commerce marketing, emphasizing cross-channel checks, identifying conversion latency, and mathematically isolating the specific variables (e.g., AOV, conversion rate, impressions) causing a decline. modules: [MEA] topics: [business and marketing analytics, conversion rate optimization, attribution and modeling] tier: 2 scope_hint: core

Topics. business and marketing analytics / Executing a top-down root cause analysis framework to diagnose e-commerce performance declines, moving from business-level KPIs (revenue, profit) down to channel checks, campaign types, and individual sub-metrics (e.g., CTR, AOV). Debunking the urge to start troubleshooting at the ad level, demonstrating that a drop in a sub-metric (like a specific ad's CPC) is irrelevant if it does not mathematically impact the top-line revenue equation: Revenue = Conversion Rate × Average Order Value × Sessions. Isolating the specific lever causing a revenue dip: determining if the issue lies in AOV (product mix/upsells), conversion rate (landing page/offer), or sessions (traffic volume). attribution and modeling / Diagnosing attribution latency, specifically within Google Ads, where conversions are retroactively attributed to the day of the click rather than the day of the purchase. Preventing premature panic and unnecessary account changes by evaluating performance using the "conversions by conversion time" metric to gain an accurate read on recent days, rather than relying on default delayed attribution. Correlating attributed platform numbers with true "base reality" business KPIs (e.g., MER/AMER) to confirm if a reported dip is an actual business failure or merely a tracking/attribution error. conversion rate optimization / Investigating the factors that depress website conversion rates after traffic hits the landing page. Conducting structured audits to determine if a conversion rate drop is caused by broken tracking, material landing page alterations (e.g., price changes, broken redirects, merchandising shifts), audience mismatch (e.g., bidding on irrelevant search terms), learning phase resets, or the termination of a strong promotional offer. Emphasizing the need to isolate CRO variables during testing rather than applying multiple fixes simultaneously (the "kitchen sink" approach), which confounds the data and obscures which specific change actually solved the problem.

Look for. The fundamental rule before starting any root cause analysis: check the change history first to ensure a recent tweak isn't causing the issue. The revenue equation used to isolate performance drops: Revenue = Conversion Rate × Average Order Value × Sessions. The definition of conversion latency in Google Ads: conversions are retroactively attributed to the day of the click, making the most recent 3–4 days always look artificially poor unless measured by "conversion time." The definition of the "kitchen sink" approach: making multiple simultaneous fixes to a landing page or campaign, which obscures which specific change actually resolved the issue.
